newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - March 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - March 7.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Management of Franco-Ivorian security firm CODIVAL, which transports cash between Ivory Coast's banks, locks out striking workers until they agree to return to work; strike began on Wednesday over working conditions.
- Ivory Coast's president, Henri Konan Bedie, guest of honour at Ghana's 40th birthday celebrations.
- Ivory Coast's newly privatised telecommunication company CI-TELCOM says it will soon start charging customers extra for calls made to cellular telephone networks.

- Leaders of student federation FESCI reach agreement with authorities at Ivory Coast's universities after weeks of tension and protest; call for resumption of classes from Monday after two sides hold talks and student leaders secure postponement of certain examinations.

- West African director of German Cooperation Ministry Christian W. Potyka says large commercial plantations are operating illegally in protected forest in Abengourou area of north eastern Ivory Coast but that agriculture ministry is working to end the practice in months or years ahead; Germany funds forest protection in Ivory Coast and has made departure of illegal plantations a condition of continued aid.
- Head of Ivorian customs Adama Coulibaly tells seminar for officials of office that monitors freight shipments to and from Ivory Coast that customs fraud is a major problem.
- Newly privatised telephone company CI-TELCOM says vandals broke fibre-optic telephone link between commercial capital.

Abidjan and second city of Bouake via capital Yamoussoukro; apologises for disruption and says repair work under way - Members of opposition Rally of the Republicans say commission of inquiry into bloody protests that surrounded Ivory Coast's 1995 presidential election show bias and disdain and seem bent on revenge and humiliating opposition activists.
- Magistrates and their unions say former justice minister Faustin Kouame allowed four trainee magistrates among 56 who take oath of office today Friday to train without proper qualifications.
- Man burnt alive in Abidjan's Koumassi suburb after crowd accused him of making penises shrink or disappear
